claims.text: On 7 August 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services approved Governor Ferguson's request to declare a federal Public Health Emergency in response to the Eastern Washington wildfires, covering the same six counties (Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Yakima) and three tribal nations (Yakama Nation, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Spokane Tribe of Indians) already covered by the 4 August 2026 federal emergency declaration.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 7 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson's office announced that the US Department of Health and Human Services approved his request to declare a Public Health Emergency for the wildfire-affected areas of Eastern Washington -- Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties, plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. This is a second, stacked federal declaration alongside the major disaster/emergency declaration Washington received on 4 August 2026. No death or displacement figures have been published on an allowlisted source.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 10 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson signed an emergency proclamation suspending numerous state laws to help those affected by the wildfires, now covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Douglas and Yakima counties plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians (adding Douglas County to the area covered by the 4 August federal emergency declaration). The Governor's office states: "My emergency proclamation waives and suspends numerous state laws so that help can move quickly," and the proclamation suspends disaster cash assistance eligibility requirements, personal document replacement fees, professional license renewal deadlines, unemployment benefit waiting periods and job-search requirements, a two-week limitation on eviction-related actions, healthcare provider licensing and supervision requirements, hospital and pharmacy licensing restrictions, and adult family home/assisted living facility capacity limitations, and waives late fees for employers unable to file or pay second-quarter 2026 taxes because of the wildfires. No death toll, injury count, acreage, containment, or displacement figures are given in this release.

InciWeb (the US federal wildland fire agencies' official incident-information system), Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated Tuesday 11 August 2026, 10:46 p.m. PT: the Sinlahekin Fire -- now the state's largest -- stands at 150,241 acres and 42% contained, with 1,541 personnel assigned and an estimated containment date of 19 August 2026; current guidance for nearby residents is to 'Stay ready to evacuate if conditions change.'

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated 12 August 2026 21:34 PT: the fire stands at 152,921 acres and 37% contained (up from 150,241 acres / 42% contained on 11 August), with 1,593 personnel assigned (up from 1,541) and an estimated containment date of 19 August 2026; evacuation guidance remains 'Stay ready to evacuate if conditions change.'

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated Thursday 13 August 2026, 9:26 p.m. PT: acreage 151,850 acres, containment 42% (up from 37% on 12 August; acreage essentially unchanged from 152,921), 1,600 personnel assigned (up from 1,593), estimated containment date 19 August 2026.

InciWeb (update posted 15 August 2026, 10:31 PM): the Sinlahekin Fire has grown to 152,682 acres and is 42% contained (1,677 personnel assigned), with an estimated full-containment date of 19 August 2026; the fire started 26 July 2026 from a lightning strike about 12 miles west of Tonasket, WA.

published.description: Dozens of wildfires broke out across the Pacific Northwest in late July and early August 2026, scorching hundreds of thousands of acres and forcing large-scale evacuations across eastern Washington State and into Idaho. On 1 August 2026 Washington Governor Bob Ferguson proclaimed a statewide wildfire emergency, and on 4 August 2026 President Trump approved a federal emergency declaration authorizing FEMA to coordinate federal disaster relief for Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. NOAA's GOES-West satellite has been used to monitor the resulting smoke plumes across the region. No allowlisted source has yet published a confirmed death toll, structure-loss count, or precise evacuation figure; the fires remained only minimally contained as of the federal declaration. Re-checked 9 August 2026: on 7 August 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services approved Governor Ferguson's request for a federal Public Health Emergency declaration covering the same six Washington counties and three tribal nations already under the 4 August federal emergency declaration. NOAA's most recent wildfire-specific coverage (4 August 2026) remains unchanged. On 7 August 2026, a federal Public Health Emergency declaration (HHS, via the Governor's office) was added on top of the 4 August major disaster/emergency declaration, covering the same six-county and tribal-nation area. claims.text: On 25 June 2026 a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.

OCHA's Situation Report #22 (15 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,829 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

OCHA's Situation Report #23 (16 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,930 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes, with more than 1,308 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. The additional appeal was raised to US$299 million, still targeting 1.3 million people over six months. EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib conducted a field visit to La Guaira together with the UN Humanitarian Coordinator to review response efforts.

OCHA's Situation Report #24 (17 July 2026, 8:00 pm) states that, twenty-three days since the earthquakes, authorities report an official toll of 5,069 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,331 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report #26 (19 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 5,208 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,388 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes. An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months, on top of the US$632 million 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

Situation Report No. 28, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 21 July 2026, Time: 9:00 pm. Authorities report 1,405 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,346 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. The US$299 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan complements the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, increasing the target population from 5.5 million to 6.2 million people and raising total funding requirements from US$632 million to US$931 million.

Situation Report No. 30, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 23 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm. Authorities report 1,463 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. Starting with this edition, the report will be published on a weekly basis. The next edition will be released on 30 July.

OCHA Situation Report #31, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 31 July 2026, 5:00 pm: authorities report 1,500 aftershocks since the 24 June doublet earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). Official toll: 5,546 people dead and 16,740 injured; 17,907 people lost their homes. As of 30 July, 207,700 people (54% women and girls) have accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance. The additional US$299 million appeal remains in place, complementing the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan for combined requirements of US$931 million targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. The report continues to be published weekly.
Re-checked 2 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Situation Report #32 has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.

OCHA's 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' series remains at #31 (31 July 2026), with no #32 yet published; the official toll therefore remains unchanged at 5,546 dead and 16,740 injured.
The USGS is assessing earthquake-triggered landslide hazards generated by the 2026 Venezuela earthquake sequence.

International Medical Corps' Venezuela Earthquakes Situation Report #5 (published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: 'Official figures have confirmed 6,125 fatalities, 16,740 injuries and 17,907 people who have lost their homes' -- an increase in the confirmed death toll from the 5,546 recorded in OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026), while injury and homelessness figures are unchanged.

Authorities also reported that approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and that more than 1,076 aftershocks have been recorded, with at least seven (7) states impacted and La Guaira remaining the most affected state.

OCHA's Situation Report #15 (08 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,811 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and more than 1,100 aftershocks have been recorded. OCHA's Situation Report #18 (11 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency; 1,171 aftershocks have been recorded, 17,907 people remain without housing, and 315 of those who died have yet to be identified. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan; an additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report No. 20 (13 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that, nineteen days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,561 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency, with more than 1,254 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed. The response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected populations, with a capacity of 25,064 people and a current occupancy of 20,231 people. A preliminary UNDP estimate indicates direct physical damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 percent of GDP, alongside the earlier UNDRR estimate of approximately US$37 billion. The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to US$200 million.

OCHA's Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

claims.text: UN News (citing OHCHR/UN High Commissioner Volker Turk), reporting on Yemen: 'at least 17 civilians were killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas since August 6, 2026.' Specific incidents cited: a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Ma'rib (7 August) injuring six civilians including a child; missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port in Ta'izz Governorate (9 August) killing three port workers and injuring four others; and an attack on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (11 August) killing four crew members (three Pakistani nationals, one Indonesian) with additional injuries. Turk said: 'I call on all parties to de-escalate tensions and spare the Yemeni people from further misery' and 'These attacks must end immediately.'

UN News, Security Council coverage (13 August 2026): UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg briefed the Security Council warning Yemen 'faces a more serious risk of return to large-scale conflict than at any point since' the 2022 UN-mediated truce, citing intensifying military activity along the frontline and pressure on regional trade and energy flows. UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher told the Council more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity, and with the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded, 'rations are cut, clinics close and protection services disappear'; both officials called for the immediate release of 73 UN colleagues still arbitrarily detained by the Houthis.

published.description: Yemen's conflict sharply escalated from early August 2026, with Houthi (Ansar Allah) missile and drone attacks on government-held areas and shipping intensifying to a level the UN says puts the country at its highest risk of returning to large-scale war since the April 2022 truce. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said at least 17 civilians were killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas since 6 August 2026, citing a series of incidents: a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Marib on 7 August that injured six civilians including a child; missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port in Ta'izz Governorate on 9 August that killed three port workers and injured four others; and an attack on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on 11 August that killed four crew members (three Pakistani nationals and one Indonesian) and injured others. Turk called on all parties to de-escalate and warned 'these attacks must end immediately.' Briefing the UN Security Council on 13 August 2026, UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg warned Yemen faces a more serious risk of returning to large-scale conflict than at any point since the 2022 truce, citing intensifying military activity along the frontline and pressure on regional trade and energy flows; UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher told the Council more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity, with the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded. Strikes on Marib and Mokha continued through mid-August, further straining a country where, per the UN, roughly 20 million people already require humanitarian assistance.
